source_span: We now expect two additional 25bp rate hikes in December and March, bringing the target range to 4.25-4.5%. The repeated language around removing accommodation, mentions of geopolitical risks, and a revision up of the neutral rate in the projections all leaned hawkish.
source_chain: Warsh called the September hike a removal of 'a dose of accommodation,' said financial conditions are still not restrictive, cited geopolitical/inflation risk, and the dot plot's neutral-rate estimate rose to 3.25% from 3.06% (i.e. any given rate restrains the economy less than assumed) — therefore MS revises its call from one remaining hike to two (December, March) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal — therefore an October hike is also plausible if Warsh pushes it, but the whole path breaks (one-and-done in December, or none) if the Middle East conflict de-escalates or disinflation is faster than expected.
pulse_chain: Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, Warsh calls it removing 'a dose of accommodation,' says policy is still not restrictive, flags upside inflation risk, and the neutral-rate dot rises to 3.25% from 3.06% (any given rate restrains less than assumed) — therefore banks split on how much more tightening is real: MS (two more, Dec/March, to 4.25-4.50%) and SocGen (75bp total) sit on one side, while Goldman (house view the Fed underdelivers vs. the four hikes priced, closer to two, terminal held at 3.25-3.50% on expected 2027 cuts) and HSBC (2-3 hikes as the sensible ceiling) sit on the other — therefore next Friday's payrolls, the last major print before the October meeting, decides the near-term path, with MS's own invalidation preserved: faster Middle East de-escalation or disinflation makes December the last hike rather than the first of several.
why: The pulse reproduces MS's premise (Warsh's accommodation language, the neutral-rate dot revision), MS's revised conclusion (two hikes to 4.25-4.50%), and MS's own invalidation (Middle East de-escalation/faster disinflation caps it at one hike) without reversing any step, and correctly attributes the contrasting GS/SocGen/HSBC figures to their own notes rather than blending them into MS's argument.
